items.prose: A text has 12 words, counting each full stop as a word.
items.question: How many pairs of neighbouring words does it have?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Every word but the last starts one pair.

byKey.per-word: The last word starts no pair: 12 − 1 = 11.
byKey.no-overlap: Pairs overlap, so each word but the last starts one.

explain.text: Each of the first 11 words starts one pair, so the text has 11 pairs.

items.question: What is the first word's chance at temperature $\tfrac12$? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Square both, add, then divide.

byKey.no-rescale: 0.36 is the square. Divide it by the total of the squares, 0.52.
byKey.same: 0.6 is the chance at temperature 1. Square and rescale.

explain.text: The squares are 0.36 and 0.16, which add to 0.52. So the first word has $0.36 \div 0.52 \approx 0.692$: sharper than 0.6.

items.prose: A trader's log reads `buy sell buy buy sell hold buy`.
items.question: How many times does “sell” come straight after “buy”?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Look one word to the right of each “buy”.

byKey.backwards: 1 is the count of “sell buy”, the pair the wrong way round.
byKey.buys: 4 counts every “buy”. Count only those followed by “sell”.

explain.text: The pairs are `buy sell`, `sell buy`, `buy buy`, `buy sell`, `sell hold` and `hold buy`. So `buy sell` appears 2 times.

items.prose: A row has chances up 0.4, flat 0.25, down 0.35, in that order. A draw gives $u = 0.65$.
items.question: Which word does it pick?

options.why: flat's running total is exactly 0.65, which is not above 0.65. Walk on.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the first running total above 0.65.

explain.text: The running totals are 0.4, 0.65 and 1. 0.65 is not above 0.65, so the first total above $u$ is 1: down.

items.question: What is the chance of the first word? Give a decimal.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide 6 by the row total.

byKey.count: 6 is the count. Divide it by the row total, 10.
byKey.even: You shared the chance evenly between three words. Divide 6 by 10.

explain.text: The row total is $6 + 3 + 1 = 10$, so the first word has $\tfrac6{10} = 0.6$.

items.prose: A model splits text into single characters.
items.question: How many tokens is “stockholders”?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count one token per character.

byKey.pieces: 3 is the pieces stock, hold and ers. This model reads characters.
byKey.word: As a word it is one token; as characters it is 12.

explain.text: s, t, o, c, k, h, o, l, d, e, r, s: 12 characters, so 12 tokens.

items.prose: Letters can be tokens too. In a list of 32,033 names, the letter n appears 18,327 times, and 6,763 of those end the name.
items.question: What is the chance that a name ends straight after an n? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide by the times n appears: the row total.

byKey.names: You divided by the 32,033 names. The row for n holds the 18,327 times n appears.

explain.text: The row for n holds 18,327 pairs, and 6,763 of them are n then the end. So the chance is $\tfrac{6763}{18327} \approx 0.369$.

items.prose: A writer always takes the most likely next word, with no random number.
items.question: Why does it soon repeat itself?

options.text: Each word always leads to the same next word
Its table has too few words to choose from
options.why: A large table loops too: the top word after each word never changes.

options.text: Its random numbers repeat after a while
options.why: This writer uses no random number at all.

feedback.correct: Each word always leads to the same word, so it loops.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Think about what the top word does.

explain.text: With no random number, each word always leads to its top word. Once a word comes round again, the run repeats from there.

items.prose: A row has chances 0.64 and 0.36. Their square roots are 0.8 and 0.6.
items.question: What is the first word's chance at temperature 2? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide 0.8 by the total of the roots.

byKey.no-rescale: 0.8 is the root alone. Rescale by the total, 1.4.
byKey.squared: That is temperature $\tfrac12$. Temperature 2 takes roots.

explain.text: The roots add to $0.8 + 0.6 = 1.4$, so the first word has $0.8 \div 1.4 \approx 0.571$: flatter than 0.64.

items.prose: A share's moves over 8 days: `up up down up down down up up`.
items.question: What is the chance that a down day follows a down day? Give a fraction.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the pairs that start with down.

byKey.words: $\tfrac38$ is the share of all 8 days that were down. Use the pairs that start with down.
byKey.even: You split evenly between up and down. Count the pairs: up 2, down 1.

explain.text: The pairs that start with down are `down up`, `down down` and `down up`. One of the three goes on to down, so the chance is $\tfrac13$.
